summary:
Turn 3 opened the next Candidate and closed two recovery reachability questions on sources.

State on entry. The map stands at audit spec v2 with core_overview usable, the previous PreAccept wrong-slot Candidate closed as explained, pending_work empty, and next_objective investigate_and_refocus.

Resolved this turn (recorded in feedback). handlePrepareReply's sub-case 3 guard is textually identical to sub-case 4's (preAcceptCount >= SlowQuorumSize-1 && !leaderResponded && allEqual), so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs. Since bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4 (epaxos.go:1306), the whole TryPreAccept path is dead: handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply, the possibleQuorum bookkeeping and the deferMap defer-cycle check. The possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] counting error therefore has no reachable consequence, and the missing sub-case is conservative rather than unsafe -- weaker pre-accept support falls to sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value or NOOP. Together with the previously explained PreAccept branch, the reachability questions around recovery and pre-accept are answered from the guard text and the single call site, without execution.

New Candidate (safety, priority 3). handlePreAcceptReply discards the reply-wise equality result for r.N <= 3 with Thrifty, so inst.lb.allEqual keeps its initial true, and with FastQuorumSize = 2 for N = 3 the commit condition (preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) is met by a single reply whose recomputed (seq, deps) may differ from the leader's. The Candidate asks whether that can leave two attribute vectors for one instance at the same vbal -- the leader's committed vector and the peer's pre-accepted vector -- so that a later recovery, which keeps the reply with the highest vbal while iterating the reply slice (element.VBallot >= lb.ballot), can re-commit the peer's vector instead of the committed one, with the legal crash point between the local fast commit and bcastCommit. Importance is agreement and state-machine convergence: one instance committed with different dependency vectors would order the same command differently on different replicas. Discriminators, the alternative author argument (a majority fast quorum may be thought to make equality unnecessary), and the vbal bookkeeping asymmetry (the fast-commit branch sets bal but not vbal, while handleAccept sets vbal = accept.Ballot) are all recorded; no requirement, premise or history was weakened, and no formal execution was submitted.
